newsitem.title: USA: Colombia's Cusiana buyers told possible Sept delay.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Cusiana buyers told possible Sept delay.

text.p: Buyers of Colombia's Cusiana crude oil are being told that September loadings could experience some delays, apparently the result of operational hiccups as the field ramps up production, traders said on Friday.
"There are potential delays in Cusiana," a Gulf Coast buyer said. "There's not as much oil as they thought. They're talking a couple of days (delay). It's all very tentative right now."
Another buyer concurred. "Things have been tied up for months," he said. "There's clearly something funny going on."
British Petroleum, which operates the Cusiana/Cupiagua complex in the Andean foothills, was not immediately available for comment.
Officials from state oil company Ecopetrol were also unavailable for immediate comment.

The original September program, which consists of 15 cargoes, including a cross-month shipment loading September 29 to October 3, marked a dramatic increase from the August program of 10 cargoes and a previous monthly average of seven.
The bulk of the September cargoes have already been sold to U.S. refiners. Traders said that the remaining two or three cargoes may be removed from the program.
The possible delays appear to reflect a one-month setback in the scheduled ramp-up of Cusiana production, which is now running around 215,000 barrels per day (bpd).
A target of 320,000 bpd that was supposed to be reached at the end of July or early August was pushed back to late August or early September.
Similarly, a peak 500,000 bpd was pushed back to late January or early February from a late-December-early January target.

Threats against contract workers from leftist rebels caused a one-month delay in construction work in June. BP, however, has said the delay was a result of the need for further testing on the new Ocensa pipeline that carries Cusiana crude to the Caribbean port of Coveqas.
